mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% over the previous three months signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% MoM and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS growth and UNRATE decrease on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous three months signals a strong labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances with PAYEMS growth, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals a favorable environment for corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of INDPRO growth and low FEDFUNDS on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
